title: What Are the Biological Methods to Purify Tub or Pot Soil?
content: Biological soil purification methods include mixing compost (about one-fifth of the soil volume) to increase organic matter, nutrients, and water-holding capacity. Vermicompost at 5–10% improves nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium levels, supporting healthy plant growth.

title: How Do Beneficial Microorganisms Help Purify Tub Soil?
content: Beneficial organisms like Trichoderma reduce soil-borne pathogens, Mycorrhizal fungi enhance root growth, and bacteria such as Azospirillum or Rhizobium fix nitrogen. These should be applied according to packet instructions.

title: Can Green Manure Improve Soil Quality in Tubs?
content: Green manure materials such as lentils, barley, lupine, grass clippings, or decomposed kitchen waste like lemon peels and coffee grounds improve soil fertility, soften soil texture, and increase beneficial microbial activity.

title: What Are Simple Biological Ways to Disinfect Tub Soil?
content: Soil can be biologically disinfected by mixing neem oil cake or Trichoderma into the soil. Solarization by covering moist soil with polythene and exposing it to strong sunlight raises temperatures to 50–60°C, killing pathogens, insects, and weed seeds.

title: What Precautions Should Be Taken During Tub Soil Purification?
content: Avoid mixing too many organic materials at once, as it can make the soil heavy and poorly aerated. Organic inputs should be mixed 1–2 weeks before planting to allow proper decomposition and microbial balance.
